source_title: Manisha becomes first-ever Indian woman to win gold medal at Wrestling World Championships - Sportstar
source_excerpt:
Manisha Bhanwala (in pic) is only the second Indian wrestler after Sushil Kumar (66kg, 2010 Moscow) to win a gold medal at the Wrestling World Championships. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
Manisha Bhanwala created history in Astana, Kazakhstan, on Friday as she became the first-ever Indian woman to win a gold medal at the Wrestling World Championships.
The 29-year-old Manisha came from behind to defeat USA’s Abigail Nette 8-6 in a thrilling 59kg final.
Manisha overcame her disappointing performance in the 57kg weight class at the Asian Games in Japan to give a dominating performance in the non-Olympic category.
“I’ve been waiting for a long time for this moment,” Manisha said. “From 2022, I’ve been writing that I would be world champion. This was my dream that I would be the first Indian woman to become a world champion. Today that dream has come true. I want to continue with this dream.”
Manisha began her campaign with a ‘Victory By Fall’ over Canada’s Laurence Beauregard in the round of 16. In the quarterfinals, the Indian took down Mongolia’s Bolortuya Khurelkhuu with a 6-0 scoreline. In the semifinals, the wrestler from Haryana defeated local favourite Altyn Shagayeva via technical superiority.
In the final, Manisha suffered an early setback as Nette quickly executed a four-point move. The Indian challenged that call only to lose and give another point to the American. A caution against Manisha extended Nette’s advantage to 6-0. But Manisha got a stepout before the break to get one point on board.
In the second period, Manisha started her comeback with a takedown against Nette. The 28-year-old American challenged arguing that the referee had whistled to stop the bout. The unsuccessful challenge awarded one more point to Manisha and position in par terre.
From 6-4, Manisha managed to turn Nette using a gut-wrench for two points. She even tried holding the American for the fall but could not execute it.
“ Bharandaaj [gut-wrench] is my favorite move,” she said. “It’s been my favourite for some time now. When I got that move, I felt I was going to get to 10 points just like that or even pin her. But she got out of that position. At that time I thought, how did that happen? Then when the bout restarted I got her down.”
At 6-6, Nette was still ahead based on the criterion of a bigger scoring move and tried to run down the clock. However, Manisha scored another takedown and held on to her 8-6 lead to create history.
Manisha is only the second Indian wrestler after Sushil Kumar (66kg, 2010 Moscow) to win the gold medal at the prestigious tournament.
At the ongoing edition, Manisha is the fourth Indian medallist in women’s wrestling after Neelam Sirohi (silver, 50kg), Kajal Dhochak (silver, 76kg) and Tanu Sharma (bronze, 72kg).
In men’s freestyle, Vicky (97kg) was beaten 10-0 by Iranian superstar Hassan Yazdani in the repechage round.
Three others, Nikhil (61kg), Pushpender Dalal (86kg) and Jaspooran Singh (125kg), moved into repechage rounds.
